Fourth Fitna.subject: Defence & Security
Fourth Fitna.question: He then demanded of his brother the cession of the western regions of _____, the admission of caliphal tax and postal agents into the province, and the forwarding of Khurasan's revenue to Baghdad
Fourth Fitna.fact: After al-Ma'mun, fearing for his safety, refused, al-Amin began to interfere with his brother's domain: he protested al-Ma'mun's pardon to Ibn al-Layth after his surrender and asked for tribute from the governors of the western provinces of Khurasan as a sign of submission. Fourth Fitna.subject: Defence & Security
Fourth Fitna.question: Under the influence of their respective chief ministers, al-_____ and al-Ma'mun took steps that further polarized the political climate and made the breach irreparable
Fourth Fitna.fact: Under the influence of their respective chief ministers, al-Amin and al-Ma'mun took steps that further polarized the political climate and made the breach irreparable. After al-Ma'mun symbolically removed al-Amin's name fro.

Fourth Fitna.subject: Defence & Security
Fourth Fitna.question: The news of Ali's approach threw _____ into panic, and even al-Ma'mun considered fleeing
Fourth Fitna.fact: Despite the reservations of some of his senior ministers and governors, two months later, in January 811, al-Amin formally began the civil war when he appointed Ali ibn Isa governor of Khurasan, placed him at the head of an unusually large army of 40,000 men, drawn from the abnaʾ, and sent him to depose al-Ma'mun. When Ali ibn Isa set out for Khurasan, he reportedly took along a set of silver chains with which to bind al-Ma'mun and carry him back to Baghdad.

Fourth Fitna.fact: Tahir now advanced westwards, defeated another abnaʾ army of 20,000 under Abd al-Rahman ibn Jabala after a series of hard-fought engagements near Hamadan, and reached Hulwan by winter.

Fourth Fitna.fact: Al-Amin now desperately tried to bolster his forces by alliances with Arab tribes, notably the Banu Shayban of Jazira and the Qays of Syria.

Fourth Fitna.fact: He invaded Khuzistan, where he defeated and killed the Muhallabid governor Muhammad ibn Yazid, whereupon the Muhallabids of Basra surrendered to him.
